key_findings.finding: This presentation is clinical tension pneumothorax requiring immediate right-sided decompression without waiting for imaging. Needle thoracostomy is a temporizing maneuver; definitive treatment is tube thoracostomy (or immediate finger/open thoracostomy followed by chest tube when trained personnel and equipment are available).

source_tools.relevance: 2021 review identifies emergent needle thoracostomy as an adjunct for tension pneumothorax in trauma; 2012 evidence describes tube thoracostomy as the gold-standard treatment.

key_findings.finding: For an adult, current ATLS-oriented guidance favors decompression at the 4th–5th intercostal space at the anterior axillary or midaxillary line, rather than relying only on the traditional 2nd intercostal space midclavicular site. Insert immediately above the superior border of the rib to avoid the intercostal neurovascular bundle.

source_tools.relevance: The 2019 paper explicitly reports ATLS 10th-edition guidance favoring the 4th/5th intercostal space at the midaxillary line in adults; the 2025 consensus/meta-analysis supports the 5th intercostal space at the midaxillary line or 2nd intercostal space midclavicular line.

key_findings.finding: If the question asks for the single best immediate intervention/site: perform right needle decompression at the 5th intercostal space, anterior-to-midaxillary line (using an appropriately long catheter), then immediately place a right tube thoracostomy in the 4th–5th intercostal space within the safe triangle. The 2nd intercostal space, midclavicular line remains an accepted alternative in some protocols, but is not the preferred current ATLS adult site.

source_tools.relevance: Directly supported by the ATLS 10th-edition summary and current consensus recommendation in the search results.
The review search results distinguish needle decompression from definitive tube thoracostomy and report tube thoracostomy as the gold standard.
